entities.summary:
Fadrique Álvarez de Toledo y Enríquez, 2nd Duke of Alba was a Spanish nobleman, military leader and politician. He played a pivotal role in the Italian Wars, commanding Spanish forces in Italy and Naples from 1503 to 1508. During his tenure, he implemented various reforms and expanded Spanish influence in the region.

Álvarez de Toledo was a key figure in the Spanish Monarchy, serving as a regent for his niece, Juana I of Castile, and later as a member of the Council of State. He also played a crucial role in the Reconquista, leading Spanish forces to several victories against Moorish armies in the Iberian Peninsula.

Despite his significant contributions to Spanish politics and military affairs, Álvarez de Toledo's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by that of his more famous contemporaries, such as Charles V and Ferdinand II of Aragon. Nevertheless, his impact on Spanish history and culture is undeniable.

The 2nd Duke of Alba's life and career serve as a testament to the complex and often tumultuous nature of 16th-century Spanish politics. His experiences during the Italian Wars and his role in shaping the Spanish Monarchy provide valuable insights into the workings of the Iberian Peninsula during this period.
